newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh floods cut roads, raise health fears.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh floods cut roads, raise health fears.

text.p: Hundreds of volunteers and doctors waded through flooded villages in northern Bangladesh on Tuesday to deliver water purifying tablets to people affected by a deluge that has already claimed 20 lives, local officials said.

They said some 200 people had been infected with diarrhoea in Rajshahi and Chaipainawabganj districts, where around 300 houses had been washed away by waters from the flooded Padma and Mahananda rivers.
Dr. Binod Bihari Saha, civil surgeon in Chapainawabganj, told Reuters on Tuesday that 32 medical teams were working in the district to prevent an epidemic of water-borne diseases.

Dr Wasim Hossain, deputy civil surgeon in Rajshahi, said his office had mobilised an emergency stock of 225,000 water purifying tablets and 175,000 packets of oral rehydration saline to be handed out to flood victims.

He quoted Rajshahi district officials as saying that the week-long floods had killed at least 20 people and affected over half a million. Most of those killed drowned and some died when their houses collapsed, the officials said.
"The situation is getting worse every moment with the rivers still rising and rain battering the affected areas," Mohammad Abdul Muhaymen, a local journalist, told Reuters.
Road links between Chapainawabganj and rest of the country have remained cut since Monday, restricting relief and medical operations, local officials told reporters.
They said nearly 15,000 hectares (37,500 acres) of rice and other crops have been damaged in Rajshahi alone.

New floods triggered by heavy rain and a rush of floodwater from neighbouring India struck Bangladesh's northern districts last week while they were still recovering from floods in May that killed at least 65 people.
The Flood Information Centre in Dhaka said the overall flood situation was expected to deteriorate.
The Padma, already threatening Rajshahi city's protective embankment, swelled five cm (two inches) on Tuesday and was flowing 25 cm (10 inches) above its danger mark, local officials said.
Newspapers said on Tuesday that thousands of riverside villagers were awaiting evacuation.
